title: Apt-Serve: Adaptive Request Scheduling on Hybrid Cache for Scalable LLM Inference Serving
technique: hybrid cache (KV cache + memory-efficient hidden-state cache) to enlarge batch size, plus adaptive batch-composition scheduling that maximizes reduction of total pending time subject to a cache memory constraint (with SLO-aware demotion of violated requests)

optimized_metrics.evidence: We focus on improving the effective throughput of LLM inference services, which currently experience performance bottlenecks due to the rapid decline in TTFT SLO attainment as the request rate increases.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Time To First Token (TTFT), measuring the duration of the prefill phase; ii) Time Between Tokens (TBT), quantifying the time between consecutive token generations during the decode phase.
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT described as prefill phase duration but SLO violations are attributed to queueing/pending delays, so TTFT effectively includes waiting

metric_definitions.definition_quote: P99 TBT refers to the 99th percentile of TBT latency for each individual request, where the generation of one output token in the decode phrase contributes to a TBT latency value
metric_definitions.notes: per-request P99 over that request's token gaps, then request counted as meeting SLO if its own P99 TBT <= SLO

metric_definitions.definition_quote: effective throughput [12, 62, 89] which is defined as the highest sustainable online request rate that meets specified SLOs attainment criteria, such as serving at least 70% of requests within the target SLOs of (TTFT=1 second, 99th percentile TBT=1 second)
metric_definitions.notes: max request rate (req/s) at an attainment level (90% attainment used in §3.1 example; 70% in intro example)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The SLO attainment rate is calculated by the number of served user requests that satisfy both TTFT and P99 TBT SLOs divided by the total number of requests during the whole serving process.

slo_spec: Application-driven SLOs (Table 3): TTFT / P99 TBT in s - ShareGPT 13B 1.0/1.0, 30B 1.5/1.0, 66B 2.0/1.0; HumanEval 0.5/0.5, 1/0.5, 1.5/0.5; LongBench 4.0/1.0, 4.5/1.0, 5.0/1.0 (set by principle of prior work [89]: TTFT relaxed for long prompts and grows with model size). Attainment threshold used to read effective throughput (e.g. 90%).
load_regime: request-rate sweep (Poisson arrivals; 1,000 sampled requests per dataset)
tradeoff_acknowledged: SLO-aware demotion of violated requests starves ~10% of requests (high tail latency); trading SLO attainment against tail latency possible via a decaying factor (0.4 variant). Hidden cache adds extra linear-transform cost that slows batches (manageable extra TBT).
workloads: ShareGPT, HumanEval, LongBench (summarisation, length-limited for OPT)
extractor_notes: Optimizes effective throughput via TTFT attainment; formal scheduling objective is sum of per-request 'pending time' reduction (a queueing proxy) under a memory cap. Per-request P99 TBT is the TBT SLO statistic (not a system-wide percentile). Fig 10 'tail latency' of starved requests is a reported side effect.

tail_audit.metrics: TTFT attainment + TBT @ P99 (per-request P99 TBT <= SLO) -> SLO attainment

load_class_quote: arrivals following a Poisson distribution (§3); request-rate sweep, 1,000 sampled requests per dataset (§6)
